stories.title: Drone footage shows Mount Etna cable car above volcanic landscape
stories.summary: Sicily's Etna cable car carries visitors up Europe's active volcano while engineers manage risks from eruptions, gases and harsh conditions.

stories.title: Iraq eyes supplying Turkey with 1 million oil barrels a day amid Hormuz crisis
stories.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Zeydi visited Ankara for his first talks with Erdoğan since taking office, offering to supply Turkey with 1 million barrels of oil per day as Ankara seeks to reduce its dependence on disrupted Gulf routes.

stories.title: Iran rejects Hormuz deal and launches surprise strike on US forces in Jordan
stories.summary: Tehran rejected an Omani proposal to divide the strait equally and declared Hormuz would "never return to its prewar situation," hours before the IRGC launched multiple ballistic missiles at US forces in Jordan in what CENTCOM called an attempted surprise attack.

stories.title: Houthis to copy Iran's Hormuz playbook with Red Sea toll plan
stories.summary: Yemen's information minister said intelligence confirmed IRGC advisers were directly involved in designing a Houthi-enforced toll system for the Bab el-Mandeb, mirroring Iran's contested claim to charge fees in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Pakistan accused of fatally shooting 30 unarmed protesters in Kashmir
stories.summary: Local civil rights group alleges authorities removed evidence of killings amid communications blackout At least 30 people are alleged to have been killed in Pakistan-administered Kashmir in the past two days as part of what has been claimed is a brutal state crackdown that has engulfed the disputed region for weeks. stories.title: US bans humanoid robots from China, citing ‘unacceptable risks’
stories.summary: Move comes as the Trump administration has increasingly sought to keep Chinese technology out of the US The Federal Communications Commission announced a ban on humanoid robots from China on Tuesday, saying that the technology poses “unacceptable risks” to the country’s national security. The move comes as the Trump administration has increasingly sought to keep Chinese technology out of the US. stories.title: Kenya investigating unexpected deaths of 15 elephants in national park
stories.summary: Potential toxic substance detected in several of 15 elephants found dead in Kenya’s Amboseli national park Officials are investigating the deaths of 15 elephants over the past month in Kenya’s Amboseli national park. The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) said 10 of the elephants showed signs of partial paralysis before dying within two days. Continue reading...

stories.title: Germany's leaders say the Berlin Pride attack targeted 'all of us'. What utter hypocrisy | Fatma Aydemir

First come the flowers, then the pious statements. One after another, mainstream German politicians have lined up to claim that the attack on Berlin Pride last weekend was an attack on “all of us”, “our values” and “our society”. Except it was not. stories.title: ‘The shaking was terrifying’: stories of survival and loss emerge after Japan earthquake
stories.summary: Rescuers pulling people from the wreckage in southern Japan in a haunting repeat of disaster that struck 10 years ago ‘Race against time’: Japan earthquake death toll rises as rescue teams search for missing “There was a voice coming from the collapsed house, and I could see a hand,” Tomohide Nagata, a volunteer firefighter, told the Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbun. “One of our senior members crawled in and pulled him out. stories.title: US-Saudi strikes in Iraq push region into ‘uncharted territory’, analysts warn
stories.summary: Riyadh’s decision to join US in strikes on Iran-backed militia further complicates widening and ‘unpredictable’ war Middle East crisis – live updates US-Saudi strikes on Iran-backed militia in Iraq have pushed the region into “uncharted territory”, analysts have warned. Amid stark warnings of a widening and increasingly “unpredictable” conflict, Riyadh’s decision to publicly join the US in striking sites associated with Iraq’s Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF), killing at least 20 fighters, has

stories.title: Germany: How weather extremes impact local agriculture
stories.summary: Heat, drought, heavy rain and late frosts are taking a toll on German farmers. They increasingly respond with adapted varieties, new crops, modern breeding techniques and modified farming methods.

stories.title: How two wars and El Nino could fuel world hunger
stories.summary: The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East haven't yet crippled global food supplies. Add a powerful weather pattern like El Nino, however, and the risks multiply.

stories.title: Germany: How effective are exit programs for Islamists?
stories.summary: Germany has set up many programs to help individuals break away from the radical Islamist scene. Following the Islamist terror attack on Berlin's Pride event, critics say the programs are ineffective.

stories.title: Bayreuth Festival opens with celebration and commemoration
stories.summary: To mark its 150th anniversary, the Bayreuth Festival remembers victims of the Holocaust — and confronts its founder's antisemitism.

stories.title: German Muslims are alarmed by the Islamist terror attack in Berlin
stories.summary: Germany's Muslim organizations condemn the Islamist terrorist attack targeting Berlin's Pride celebrations and fear repercussions.

stories.title: Keiko Fujimori takes office as Peru's president, vowing to end decade of instability
stories.summary: The Popular Force leader becomes Peru's first female president, returning Fujimorism to power after 26 years. She is due to deliver her inaugural address and unveil her cabinet. King Felipe VI attended the ceremony in Lima.

stories.title: Rescuers scramble to locate survivors as death toll climbs to 13 after powerful quake hits southwestern Japan
stories.summary: Dozens more remain trapped underneath the rubble as authorities race against the clock to save as many people as possible during the critical 72 hour rescue period. The tremor is the most powerful to hit the region in 10 years since a 7.0 magnitude quake recorded in 2016.

stories.title: Japan earthquake shakes Kumamoto newsroom as staff shelter under desks
stories.summary: Footage shows newsroom staff taking cover as a magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto in southwestern Japan, killing 13 people.

stories.title: Wisconsin tornado leaves homes damaged and streets covered in debris
stories.summary: Residents in Menasha, Wisconsin, survey tornado damage as crews assess destroyed homes, fallen trees and damaged power lines after the storm.

stories.title: Dramatic California beach rescue after powerful waves hit Santa Cruz
stories.summary: A 16-year-old California lifeguard rescued a 10-year-old boy from powerful waves at Santa Cruz's Seabright State Beach in a dramatic ocean rescue.

stories.title: Syria hunts down suspects in March coastal attacks, dismantles IS cells in Aleppo
stories.summary: Security forces lured a militia commander accused of leading one of the March 2025 assault units into an ambush near Jableh, killing him and a second suspect in an exchange of fire. IS cells were separately dismantled in Aleppo and al-Bab.

stories.title: Navas del Rey residents return after Spain wildfire evacuation
stories.summary: Residents returned to Navas del Rey after Spain's wildfires, finding burned homes and scorched gardens as firefighters continued battling nearby blazes.

stories.title: Gaza residents flee before Israeli strike hits mosque area
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit Gaza City and Deir al-Balah after an evacuation warning, with footage showing explosions, flames and smoke rising into the night sky.

stories.title: More than 100 aftershocks hit Japan after powerful quake that killed 13
stories.summary: People are being urged to stay alert, with earthquake aftershocks potentially reaching magnitude 7, officials say

stories.title: France veterinary team treats pets of wildfire evacuees
stories.summary: A French veterinary team in Bordeaux is caring for pets of Gironde wildfire evacuees, providing food, treatment and support while families await their return home.

stories.title: F1 says Qatar and Abu Dhabi races remain on despite war contingency plans
stories.summary: The world's top racing competition said the final two races of the 2026 season remain on track, but a mid-September review will determine whether the championship concludes in Europe instead.

stories.title: Los Angeles hospital transformed into immersive art exhibition
stories.summary: The 'Hospital of Emotions' transforms a former Los Angeles hospital into an immersive art exhibition exploring grief, resilience and personal memories.

stories.title: 'It's our home, it's our forest': BBC speaks to locals fighting France wildfire
stories.summary: Firefighters are battling flare-ups in 40C heat in the Gironde region, as some locals have refused to heed evacuations.

stories.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to overturn €71 million defamation award in sexual assault case
stories.summary: The appeal was filed electronically and is expected to be formally docketed with the court later on Wednesday.

stories.title: More than half of England 'officially in drought', UK Environment agency says
stories.summary: "Rivers are running low, farmers are having to harvest crops early, wildfire risk is increasing, and millions of people are living under restrictions on water use," the UK Environment Agency said in its announcement.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia's dilemma as it tries to stay out of US-Iran war
stories.summary: The kingdom faces a choice of whether to keep hitting back as a deterrent or to try to de-escalate the situation.

stories.title: Audio recordings appear to show Biden discussing classified information with his ghostwriter
stories.summary: Biden was 74 when the interviews began and 81 when Hur released his report in early 2024, as he sought re-election.

stories.title: Javier Milei accuses US Democrats of financing ‘anti-Argentina campaign’ at World Cup
stories.summary: President also blames Brazil and Mexico and says online critics ‘do not want the ideas of freedom to succeed’ More than a week has passed since Ferran Torres scored the extra-time goal that gave Spain its second World Cup, but – at least for Argentina’s president – the tournament is not over. stories.title: Past fires suggest effects of Europe and North America wildfires may linger for years
stories.summary: Three years after Maui wildfires many still struggle with ‘biological, emotional and social consequences’, study says A spate of ferocious wildfires across North America and Europe, worsened by the climate crisis, has incinerated homes and forests and forced thousands of people to flee. Previous fires suggest the effects of these blazes may linger for years to come. The current fires and their plumes of smoke can appear to be a temporary, if immediate, crisis. stories.title: Canadians spent $3.3bn less on travel to US in 2025 after Trump’s return to office
stories.summary: Data shows Canadians have replaced US vacations with other international trips in apparent rebuke to Trump Canadians spent $3.3bn less on travel to the US in 2025 than in the previous year, as Donald Trump’s hostile policies towards his northern neighbour continue to incur an economic cost, new government data shows. The research also indicates that Canadians are not bucking travel overall and instead have replaced US vacations with other international destinations, in a rebuke to Trump’s tariff

stories.title: The Guardian view on noise pollution: keep it down | Editorial
stories.summary: New research linking the issue to Parkinson’s disease adds to the evidence of serious health repercussions from traffic volume and other sources The roar of late-night traffic is not just annoying for those trying to sleep. It can also have profound effects on their health. A pioneering new study, published this month, has found a clear link between road noise and Parkinson’s disease. The research, which followed more than 3 million Danish participants, found a modest but consistent effect: for

stories.title: As US-Iran war rages, who's risking the Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: Though Iran continues to attack vessels as leverage in its war with the United States, data show that several shippers continue to transit the waterway.

stories.title: Bernadette Amani 'living her dream' at Bayern and WAFCON
stories.summary: Bernadette Amani joined Bayern Munich in January and is now captaining Ivory Coast in their first WAFCON in 12 years. Getting to the top hasn't been a straight path for the newly crowned German double winner.

stories.title: Why is Germany building roads for yesterday's climate?
stories.summary: As the Autobahn buckles under heat waves, Germany is still paving roads for a past climate. Engineers know how to fix that — so what's the holdup?

stories.title: EU civil protection mechanism: Coordinating Europe's firefighters
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron has activated the EU civil protection mechanism to help combat devastating wildfires. The system has become increasingly effective, yet it will reach its limits in the summer of 2026.

stories.title: Fact check: Berlin Pride attack claims debunked
stories.summary: Following the Islamist terrorist attack at Berlin Pride, rumors, false claims and misleading videos have been spreading on social media. DW Fact check examines some of the most widely shared claims.

stories.title: FIFA plans to form new commercial subsidiary and sell stake
stories.summary: FIFA has announced plans to form a commercial subsidiary and to sell a non-controlling interest to private investors. It needs approval from member associations, but is claiming that it will benefit them financially.
